raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old woman with progressive hepatic region discomfort was referred to a hematological department in May 2006. Her previous medical history was significant for chronic aplastic anemia and she was treated with stanozolol and intermittent gamma-globulin infusion. Full blood and bone marrow examination on a regular time schedule showed significant remission.
On admission, the patient had a body temperature of 36.5  C, pulse of 75 beats per minute, blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, respiratory rate of 16 per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Her abdomen was soft to palpation. Full blood test showed leukocyte count of 3.0 x 109/L, hemoglobin 110 g/L and platelet 23 x 109/L. Immunological studies, including quantitative immunoglobulins analysis, CD4/CD8 T lymphocyte ratio, and delayed hypersensitivity skin tests, were all normal. No predisposing disease associated with immunosuppression, such as diabetes mellitus, was found. Her human immunodeficiency virus status was negative, indicating the patient was in a non-immunocompromised condition. Abdominal ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed multiple heterogeneous solid nodules in the right lobe of the liver (Figure 1). No abdominal lymphadenopathy or effusions were visible.
Malignant ailments and metastatic diseases were initially suspected, but serum tumor marker screening (including CEA, CA-125, CA-199, PSA, AFP, etc.) was within normal limits. Her aspartate aminotransferase (AST) was 80 U/L (normal range <40 U/L) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) was 65 U/L (normal range <40 U/L). Other laboratory investigations, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), galactomannan antigenemia (GM) test, and autologous antibody, performed twice a week, were not specific. Complete liver disease studies, including hepatitis virology, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus serology, urinary copper, serum ceruloplasmine failed to lead a significant result.
Two weeks after admission, ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration was performed. On histopathological examination, abundant fungal hyphae were observed in the background of necrosis and chronic inflammation (Figure 2). A. fumigatus was subsequently isolated and cultured from the biopsy aspirate. Bacterial and acid-fast smears and cultures were negative. Pulmonary aspergillosis with liver dissemination was suspected, but the patient denied relevant infectious and occupational exposure history. A comprehensive whole body evaluation, including chest and paranasal sinus computed tomography (CT), did not indicated aspergillosis lesions. Regular GM tests continued to be negative. On the basis of these findings, we concluded the diagnosis of liver aspergilloma.
The patient was prescribed caspofungin acetate (Cancidas , Merck Sharp & Dohme Pty. Ltd., Australia) according to the minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) tests. An antifungal regimen was started with caspofungin acetate 70 mg on day 1 and 50 mg daily from day 2 to day 10. Serum liver enzymes were monitored to interrupt potential adverse effects. The patient received one course of caspofungin acetate first-line therapy every month and responded well in the clinical symptoms. Two months after the initial diagnosis, repeated MRI images showed a significant reduction in the sizes and number of the liver nodules (Figure 3). Our patient underwent caspofungin acetate therapy for six months and was discharged. During our last time follow-up in May 2012, she was stable without signs of progression or recurrence.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old woman with chronic aplastic anemia in remission presented with progressive right upper quadrant hepatic discomfort.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In May 2006, the patient was referred to the hematology department for progressive discomfort in the hepatic region without fever or constitutional symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic aplastic anemia in hematological remission maintained on stanozolol and intermittent gamma-globulin infusions; no history of diabetes mellitus, HIV, or occupational fungal exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive hepatic region discomfort; afebrile and negative for respiratory or sinonasal symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vitals: temperature 36.5 C, pulse 75 bpm, blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, and SpO2 98% on room air. Abdomen was soft to palpation.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission CBC showed WBC 3.0 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin 110 g/L, and platelets 23 x 10^9/L. Liver enzymes were mildly elevated with AST 80 U/L (normal <40 U/L) and ALT 65 U/L (normal <40 U/L). Quantitative immunoglobulins, CD4/CD8 T-cell ratio, delayed-type hypersensitivity skin tests, HIV serology, viral hepatitis panel, CMV and EBV serologies, urinary copper, serum ceruloplasmin, ESR, CRP, autoantibodies, and serum tumor markers (CEA, CA-125, CA19-9, PSA, AFP) were all normal or negative. Abdominal ultrasonography showed multiple heterogeneous solid nodules in the right hepatic lobe.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal MRI confirmed multiple heterogeneous solid nodules in the right lobe of the liver without abdominal lymphadenopathy or ascites. Twice-weekly serial serum galactomannan antigenemia (GM) assays were persistently negative, and chest and paranasal sinus CT scans showed no extrahepatic fungal lesions. Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the liver lesions 2 weeks after admission demonstrated abundant fungal hyphae in a background of necrosis and chronic inflammation on histopathology, and aspirate culture isolated Aspergillus fumigatus (bacterial and AFB smears/cultures were negative).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Primary isolated hepatic aspergilloma (multiple right-lobe liver nodules caused by Aspergillus fumigatus) in a patient with remitted aplastic anemia, definitively confirmed by ultrasound-guided liver biopsy histopathology and fungal culture growing A. fumigatus (with hepatic malignancy and extrahepatic dissemination ruled out). Treated with MIC-guided intravenous caspofungin acetate (70 mg loading on day 1, then 50 mg daily on days 2-10, repeated monthly for 6 months), resulting in symptomatic resolution, marked reduction in liver nodule size and number on 2-month follow-up MRI, and sustained recurrence-free stability through 6-year follow-up in May 2012.
